chunks.arabic_text: عَلَلُ الشَّرَائِعِ: أَبِي، عَنْ سَعْدٍ، عَنِ الْبَرْقِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ بَزِيعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ بَشِيرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي حَصِينٍ، عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ، عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Ilal al-Sharai: My father, from Sa'd, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Bazi', from Ibn Bashir, from Abi Husayn, from Abi Basir, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: لَا تَكْذِبُوا بِحَدِيثٍ أَتَاكُمْ بِهِ مُرْجِيٌّ أَوْ قَدَرِيٌّ أَوْ خَارِجِيٌّ نَسَبَهُ إِلَيْنَا، فَإِنَّكُمْ لَا تَدْرُونَ لَعَلَّهُ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الْحَقِّ فَتَكْذِبُوا اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فَوْقَ عَرْشِهِ

translations.en: Do not reject a narration which is brought to you by a Murji'i or a Qadari or a Khariji which he attributes to us, for you do not know – perhaps it is something of the truth and you will be rejecting Allah, Mighty and Majestic, above His throne.

en.summary: The Imam advises believers not to dismiss hadiths attributed to them simply because the narrator belongs to a specific theological sect (Murji'i, Qadari, or Khariji). Since the truth may be present in their narration, rejecting it outright amounts to rejecting Allah Himself.
en.seo_question: Why should we not reject hadiths from specific theological sects?

key_terms.مُرْجِيٌّ: A follower of the Murji'a theological school
key_terms.قَدَرِيٌّ: A follower of the Qadariya theological school
key_terms.خَارِجِيٌّ: A follower of the Khawarij sect
